answer.text: Change in option price per Re.1 change in underlying

explanation.text: The Logic: Delta is the option Greek that measures the rate of change in the option's premium per unit change in the price of the underlying asset. For a call option, delta lies between 0 and +1; for a put, between -1 and 0. A delta of 0.5 means the option price moves approximately Re.0.50 for every Re.1 move in the underlying — making delta the primary directional-exposure measure for option positions. The Trap: Time decay is measured by theta. Sensitivity to volatility is measured by vega. Sensitivity to interest rates is measured by rho. Each Greek isolates a different driver of option value. Note: The NISM-Series-XXI-A PMS Distributors workbook (Sep 2025) covers options broadly in its derivatives chapter (pages 70-78) but does not specifically define option Greeks such as delta. The definition above is general option-pricing knowledge consistent with NISM-Series-VIII Equity Derivatives.
